Triangle quality measures

Source: R/cdt.R
cdt_quality.Rd

Per-triangle area, angles, edge lengths and radius-edge ratio, for judging a mesh or checking that refinement met its targets.

Usage

cdt_quality(x, T = NULL)

Arguments

x

a result of cdt_triangulate() (a list with P and T), or a two-column matrix of vertex coordinates, in which case T is needed

T

triangle vertex indices (m x 3, 1-based), when x is a matrix

Value

a data frame with one row per triangle and columns area (always non-negative), min_angle and max_angle (degrees), min_edge and max_edge, and radius_edge (circumradius over shortest edge; the Ruppert bound on it is about 1.41 for a 20.7 degree minimum angle, and Inf for a degenerate triangle). Use summary() on the result for the distributions.

Examples

## an irregular polygon with a sharp corner, refined by area and angle
x <- c(0, 2, 2, 1, 0)
y <- c(0, 0, 2, 0.4, 2)
r <- cdt_triangulate(x, y, 1:5, c(2:5, 1), max_area = 0.05, min_angle = 25)
q <- cdt_quality(r)
summary(q[c("area", "min_angle", "radius_edge")])
#>       area            min_angle      radius_edge    
#>  Min.   :0.008281   Min.   :26.48   Min.   :0.5979  
#>  1st Qu.:0.027521   1st Qu.:38.21   1st Qu.:0.7071  
#>  Median :0.031250   Median :42.81   Median :0.7358  
#>  Mean   :0.031579   Mean   :41.90   Mean   :0.7672  
#>  3rd Qu.:0.039806   3rd Qu.:45.00   3rd Qu.:0.8084  
#>  Max.   :0.049642   Max.   :56.75   Max.   :1.1214  
## both refinement targets were met
c(max_area = max(q$area), min_angle = min(q$min_angle))
#>    max_area   min_angle 
#>  0.04964213 26.47852647
